question.worked_solution:
First, we pull out the factor of $3$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{7x-2}{3x+1}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{7x-2}{3(x+1/3)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{7x-2}{(x+1/3)}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

|  | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $-\frac{1}{3}$ | $7$ | $-2$ |
|  | $↓$ | $-\frac{7}{3}$ |
|  | $7$ | $-\frac{13}{3}$ |

So, from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{7x-2}{(x+1/3)} & =7-\frac{(13/3)}{(x+1/3)} \\  & =7-\frac{13}{3x+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{7x-2}{3x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}(7-\frac{13}{3x+1})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[7{\int }_{0}^{1}\text{d}x-13{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{3x+1}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{[7x-\frac{13}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+1|]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[7(1-0)-\frac{13}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|4|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|1|)] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[7-\frac{13\operatorname{ln}⁡4}{3}] \\  & =\frac{7}{3}-\frac{13}{9}\operatorname{ln}⁡(4).\end{aligned}
$$
